doc: One row of one texel: the mean is the texel itself, so compose(s, fine, t) = target is solved exactly by bisection; target 0.6 with s = 0.2, scalar streak 0, no subtexel. Float32 inputs; tolerance as the typical case. Arguments: s, fine, target, streak, subtexel and offset are the inputs of that name when listed; an unlisted streak or offset (default 0.0) is the scalar in params, an unlisted subtexel is None; prm holds the GenParams fields compose reads. The 36 steps and the bracket [-10, 10] are literals of the source. Measured: promoting the float32 inputs to float64 changes the output by at most 2.2e-8; one-ulp nudges of every float input and parameter change it by at most 6.0e-8 (worst of 6 random trials); the tolerance is 75x the larger of the two spreads.
